pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts ★ on the starred item only.
'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and asserts they list in id order.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give the full list in order.

The code implements both links, but the final commit c28b524 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test now names AC-5, so by the rule that an item no test names is unmet. The state tests do check the links but do not name AC-5 either.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred; 'AC-7' test asserts it. The config check was relaxed to accept a query, with tests.

findings.what: The last commit (c28b524 'Follow-up edits', by a bot) renamed the link test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. This removes the AC-5 label, so no test names AC-5 and the item counts as unmet. The commit message hides the reason. The PR's claim that the tests cover AC-1 to AC-7 is false as a result.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-5:' prefix in the test title. Also split the check so each link is asserted on its own page.

findings.what: The PR body says test/starred.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-7, but AC-5 is no longer named in it.
findings.fix: Fix once the AC-5 label is restored.

lenses.note: The spec exists and its decisions are followed: starred items stay in id order, and the view is a query parameter with no cookie.
Every state-table row has a test. AC-5 is no longer named by any test (see finding).
The tests assert behaviour. Tests were not run here; CI runs them. The traffic test fake now records the query string, which loosens nothing. The AC-5 label was removed in the last commit.
The README describes ?show=starred. Nothing stale was found.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ cannot slip through. The SQL is built only from fixed view strings. The regex now allows ? in routes, as the PR says.
Titles are still escaped. The show value is never interpolated into SQL or HTML. No instructions were planted in the repository.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML page changed. There is no UI framework or styling, and no screenshots exist.
There is no browser in this session, and the change adds no interactive UI flow beyond two links.
The title and body match the diff, except the claim that tests cover AC-1 to AC-7.
